title: Patagonia 4-2: Multi-image blending and sky replacement in Photoshop

date.basis: embedded_creation_time metadata; transcript provides no explicit date

summary: A practical Photoshop workflow demonstration focused on blending three landscape shots with differing exposures and content into a single cohesive image, followed by a sky replacement and targeted color/tonal adjustments. The presenter walks through matching dynamic range, aligning water across shots, masking and blending with careful opacity control, correcting wide-angle distortion via resampling, and preparing a large sky layer with perspective warp. The sequence culminates in edge-conscious sky insertion, mid-tone dodging to emphasize symmetry, a 4x5 crop, subtle vignette, and finishing touches such as a blue-gold water treatment and a painterly waterfall detail painted at micron-scale brush sizes to achieve a natural look.

sections.title: Three-shot blend overview and initial exposure match
sections.description: Introduction to the problem: there are three source images on the page with varied content and exposure. The goal is to blend them into one cohesive landscape by first matching their dynamic range and planning alignment, noting differences in sharpness across lenses and frames.

sections.title: Water alignment and initial selection for blending
sections.description: The speaker begins aligning the water areas between shots, tracing whitewater to guide where to align and blend. They acknowledge color shifts (one image being bluer) and emphasize moving only the water regions to create a coherent blend while leaving other content intact.

sections.title: Opacity blending and edge refinement
sections.description: Blending continues with near-full opacity on the water areas, adjusting opacities to blend edges smoothly. The speaker notes the need to resample certain bottom areas to improve alignment and acknowledges distortion typical of wide-angle lenses.

sections.title: Mid-blend refinement and edge control
sections.description: Further refinement of the blend includes ensuring sharp edges don’t reveal edits, using hard-edge brushes at appropriate opacity, and keeping the blend believable through careful edge handling and occasional resampling adjustments.

sections.title: Sky preparation for replacement
sections.description: The workflow shifts to the sky. The presenter selects and preps a sky to replace the original, emphasizing consistent lighting direction and avoiding bright peaks that could betray a composite; notes that a wide-angle sky requires distortion considerations and a suitable selection approach.

sections.title: Sky replacement and edge integration
sections.description: The sky layer is warped and resized to fit the landscape. The presenter demonstrates moving the original landscape behind the new sky using an active inverse selection strategy, ensuring the dark edge remains prominent to prevent a cut-and-paste look and preserving mid-area detail for balance.

sections.title: Color grading, crop, and fine-detail painting
sections.description: Final touches include gentle tonal adjustments, a subtle vignette, and a blue-gold-like treatment for water. The instructor crops to a 4x5 composition, then describes painting a natural-looking waterfall with extremely small brush sizes (down to 4 pixels) and multiple illuminated channels to avoid an HDR look, emphasizing symmetry and detail in the water and rock features.

featured_techniques.technique: Match dynamic range across three shots by adjusting exposure
Water-alignment by tracing and selecting water regions for blending
Opacity-based blending and edge fading to integrate layers
Bottom-area resampling to improve blend alignment and reduce distortion
Perspective Warp to shape a wide-angle sky
Resize sky to fit landscape using layer scaling and alignment
Edge-darkening and careful inverse selection to avoid cut-and-paste look
Mid-tone dodging to emphasize symmetry and fall colors
4x5 crop and subtle tonal adjustments for final presentation
Blue-gold color treatment for water (camera calibration reference)
Fine waterfall painting with small brush (4 pixels) and multi-channel illumination
